author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: My father's family name was Pirrip, and my first name was Philip. When I was a child, I couldn't pronounce either name properly. The best I could do was call myself Pip. Because of this, everyone else started calling me Pip as well.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: I only know my father's name from reading it on his tombstone, and from what my sister, who married the blacksmith, told me. I never actually saw my parents or any pictures of them, because they died long before cameras were invented. So, everything I imagined about them came from looking at their graves.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: Based on the shape of the letters on my father's tombstone, I imagined he was a sturdy, dark-haired man. Looking at the inscription for my mother, I assumed she must have been a weak and sickly person with freckles.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: There were five small graves next to my parents' graves. These belonged to my five brothers who died when they were very young. Seeing their graves made me think they had spent their short lives lying flat on their backs.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: We lived in a marshy area near a river that led to the ocean. My older sister, Mrs. Joe Gargery, raised me, and she was very proud of the fact that she had brought me up by hand since our parents died.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: I clearly remember a cold, gray afternoon when I was standing in the churchyard. It was getting dark, and I suddenly became very aware of my surroundings and the fact that I was completely alone in the world.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: Looking at the flat, dark marshes and the nearby river, the reality of my situation hit me. I realized I was just a small, scared orphan in a large, lonely place, and I began to cry.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: Suddenly, a loud voice shouted at me to stop crying. A man stood up from behind one of the graves and threatened to cut my throat if I didn't stay quiet.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The man was wearing gray clothes and had a heavy iron chain on his leg. He was covered in mud, had no hat, and looked like he had been injured by walking through rough bushes and stones.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The man limped toward me, shivering and glaring. He grabbed me tightly by the chin and demanded that I stay completely silent while I begged him not to hurt me.
